hint.ma: Averages stacked in order from short to long mark a bullish alignment; a pullback that holds the mid-term average is a common continuation entry.
hint.ema: EMA reacts to the latest prices sooner, suited to short timeframes; compare it with the same-period MA to read momentum.
hint.boll: A narrowing band often precedes a big move; riding the upper band is not overbought in a trend.
hint.donch: Buy the upper break, sell the lower one: one of the oldest trend rules (Turtles used 20 / 55). The bands exclude the current bar, matching the backtester.
hint.vwap: The institutional cost benchmark: price above VWAP means buyers are in control. Anchors reset each trading day (UTC+8).
hint.st: Line below price is bullish, above is bearish; many traders use it directly as a trailing stop.
hint.sar: Dots below price hold longs, above hold shorts; flips often in ranges, so filter with a trend indicator.
hint.rsi: In a trend RSI can sit above 70 for a long time; a bearish divergence matters more than a plain overbought reading.
hint.macd: Histogram turning positive is the golden cross; crosses above the zero line are more reliable.
hint.kdj: J is the most sensitive line; beyond 100 or below 0 usually marks a short-term extreme.
hint.cci: Beyond ±100 is the strong zone; falling back inside from +100 is a common exit.
hint.wr: Mirror image of the KDJ K value; -20 / -80 are the usual thresholds.
hint.atr: Stops 1.5 to 2 ATR away clear normal noise; it also underpins the ticket's risk-percent sizing.
hint.volume: Volume confirms price: breakouts on volume are credible, new highs on thin volume are suspect.
hint.obv: OBV making a new high before price signals money moving in early.
hint.xmab: A user-provided indicator formula: highs and lows each get a double XMA(N); their gap widens the bands (×P1/P2) and the overbought/oversold lines (+1.2 more). Bands turn green when both step down.
hint.macandle: A partner-licensed MT4 indicator: SMA(N) is red while rising and green while falling. When the MA turns, the bar N later (signal delay) that opens and closes on the new side gets a buy/sell mark; repeated same-direction signals are skipped. Closed bars only, no repaint. Pro members only.
hint.kpsq: A partner-licensed MT4 indicator: ZigZag pivots that step up (highs) or down (lows) become resistance (green) and support (red) walls drawn from the pivot candle body to now; walls price has re-entered are dropped. Three adjustable MAs are overlaid (default 50 / 72 / 180). Closed bars only. Pro members only.
hint.shenlong: A partner-licensed MT5 indicator: double XMA(N) of highs and lows form the rails; the grey belt is an EMA(90) of weighted highs/lows. Rails vs the belt bounds classify the channel as up (red), down (green) or sideways (grey). The lower rail crossing above a bar low marks Buy, a bar high crossing above the upper rail marks Sell, with stop prices; otherwise Close Sell / Close Buy. XMA is centred, so the latest N/2 bars change as new bars arrive (as in the original). Pro members only.

unreachable.body: The admin console can't reach the backend, so users probably can't load the site either. The backend watchdog restarts it automatically within about 2 minutes: wait a few minutes, then refresh this page. If it hasn't recovered after 5 minutes, contact Rex.

hint.down: The database is unreachable and the whole site will error. Restarting the backend won't help; don't keep restarting it. Contact Rex.

hint.down: Redis isn't responding, which causes odd symptoms like "close all" finding no positions or sentiment showing "-". The watchdog notifies Rex; contact Rex.

hint.down: Direct-connect accounts can't trade right now. The VPS watchdog acts within about 90 seconds, and the gateway reconnects to the broker on its own, restarting itself within 15 minutes at most. Still red after 10 minutes usually means a broker-side problem: don't keep restarting, contact Rex.
hint.idle: The backend just started and hasn't checked the gateway yet. Wait a few seconds.

hint.down: The feed has stopped and everyone's charts are frozen. On the market-feed PC check: (1) the MT5 terminal is open and logged in; (2) the feed EA is still attached to its chart (smiley in the chart's top-right corner); (3) the "Algo Trading" toolbar button is on. This light turns green within a minute once fixed. If unsure, contact Rex.
hint.idle: The backend hasn't received a quote yet. Normal right after a restart; wait a minute.

siteDown.q: The whole site won't load, or says "cannot connect to server"
siteDown.a: The backend watchdog restarts the backend within about 2 minutes. Try again after 5 minutes; if it still fails, contact Rex.

noSignals.a: Signals are market-driven and naturally sparse in quiet markets. If none for more than half a trading day, check that the 5 signal-EA charts are still open.

gatewayDown.a: Check the "Gateway" light above. The watchdog handles it automatically; contact Rex if it's still red after 10 minutes.

reconnecting.q: Orders say "trading link reconnecting, please retry"
reconnecting.a: The gateway is reconnecting to the broker and that order was never sent. Retry in a few seconds.

unknownOutcome.q: After a restart some orders show "outcome unknown"
unknownOutcome.a: Tell the user to check their positions in MT5 first to see whether the order actually opened, before placing it again, to avoid a duplicate position.

appFrozen.q: The app shows no signals or frozen quotes, but the website is fine
appFrozen.a: Have the user fully close the app and reopen it, twice if needed.

bridgeOffline.q: A user's Bridge is offline, or says "no running MT5 terminal detected"

readOnly.a: A database quota or billing problem. Contact Rex.

server.title: Upgrade the Singapore backend server (the main one)
server.steps: 1) In the Tencent Cloud console, upgrade this 2-core 4 GB box to 4 cores 8 GB (it reboots for a few minutes — pick a quiet time); 2) in /etc/systemd/system/prismx.service.d/workers.conf change --workers 2 to --workers 4; 3) add DB_POOL_SIZE=5 and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=2 to the backend .env (4 workers × 7 = 28 connections, within Supabase's pool of 30 — without this the database refuses connections); 4) restart the backend and check this page turns green. Singapore nginx is already at worker_connections 8192.

database.title: Upgrade the Supabase database compute
database.steps: Supabase console → Project Settings → Compute and Disk: move up one size from Micro (adds a monthly cost; the database restarts for a minute or two). As users grow the database often strains together with the server; if the Database light's latency is regularly above a few dozen ms, upgrade it.

gatewayChannels.title: Add gateway query channels (the gateway on the Windows VPS)
gatewayChannels.steps: On the Windows VPS, in C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\gateway\gateway.ini set [mt5] read_channels from 2 to 4 (max 8) and double-click Restart-Gateway.cmd. Afterwards the gateway /health readBusyCount should stop climbing. Free; before switching brokers confirm the broker allows the same manager login in several places.

bridgeClient.title: Or: release a lighter Bridge (free)
bridgeClient.steps: Ask development to ship the Bridge version that reports less often while the web page is closed; once users update, each Bridge sends about a third of the check-ins and the server carries more than twice as many. It only helps after most users update.

surge.title: First check whether a crowd arrived at once
surge.steps: "Busy, please retry" mostly happens right after a signal or push, when many people open the page at the same moment; it recovers by itself within seconds to a couple of minutes. A one-off can be ignored; if it repeats within a week or happens at normal times, upgrade the server as above.

cashflowRules.title: How returns are calculated
cashflowRules.hint: Capital counts deposits only · trades below the floor don't count
cashflowRules.lead: Return = profit from counted trades ÷ capital. Weekly and monthly boards work the same way.
cashflowRules.formula: Capital = balance at period start + deposits − withdrawals this period (a withdrawal first takes this period's trading profit, only the rest reduces capital; trading profit and loss never count as capital)

case1.w: The account held 10,000 while trading; the withdrawal came later and doesn't touch a finished result.

case2.w: The money you took out never backed this trade, so it isn't used as a denominator to hold you down.

case3.t: Withdraw while a position is open
case3.w: Scored on the 10,000 it opened with: the larger moment wins, so moving money mid-trade changes nothing.

case4.t: Deposit while a position is open
case4.s: 1,000 at open → top up to 10,000 → close for 500
case4.w: Scored on the 10,000 it closed with: the larger moment again, so a deposit can't make the return look better.

case5.t: Withdraw most of it after a profit
case5.w: The withdrawal takes the 1,000 profit first, so capital is the 1,100 left in the account: withdrawing capital can't inflate the return.

cashflowRules.noteSmall: Small drops aren't withdrawals: commission, swap and similar odds and ends are ignored. A drop counts as a withdrawal only when it exceeds both 100 USD and 5% of the account's capital.

case1.s: Capital {{low}}, trading brings the balance to {{usd}}
case1.w: Capital counts deposits only, so profit can't lift you over the floor. These trades don't count, but they don't hurt the rest either.

case2.s: Deposit {{loss}} more (capital {{usd}}), then one trade earns {{gain}}
case2.w: The {{loss}} earned by the uncounted trades is in the account too, so it's included: {{gain}} ÷ ({{usd}} + {{loss}}).

case3.t: Topping up while a trade is open
case3.s: Open on {{low}} capital, deposit up to {{usd}}, then close +{{p20}}
case3.w: A trade uses the larger capital of its open and close moments, so it's {{usd}}.

case4.w: Losses don't change capital, so later trades still count.

case6.t: Withdrawing below the floor after you qualify
case6.s: Counted on {{usd}}, then withdraw down to {{low}} and keep trading
case6.w: Later wins and losses are measured on the pre-withdrawal {{usd}}; a withdrawal can't freeze your result.

case5.s: Opened last week, closed this week
case5.w: A trade belongs to the period it closes in and uses that period's capital, including any floating profit or loss carried over.

cashflowRules.noteCeiling: An account above {{usd}} USD of capital doesn't rank in this competition, including deposits past the ceiling after signing up.
cashflowRules.noteExact: This competition only accepts accounts with exactly {{usd}} USD; if deposits or withdrawals after signing up move the capital off that amount, the account doesn't rank.
cashflowRules.noteWinRate: The win-rate board is unaffected by cash flows: it only counts how many trades you won and lost.
cashflowRules.noteSealedBoard: Once a period ends its results are sealed; no later deposit, withdrawal or trade can change a finished ranking.
cashflowRules.noteSealedComp: Once a competition ends, the settled result is final; later deposits, withdrawals and trades no longer move it.
cashflowRules.noteNewPeriod: Each period starts by taking capital from the balance at that moment, so last period's profit counts as capital from this period on.

gallery.title: The 16 trading personas
gallery.lead: Tap one to read its line.

AGLZ.title: The Planner
AGLZ.say: Place the order, go make tea, let it close on its own. The only risk: starting to think you can't be wrong.

AGLM.title: The Helmsman
AGLM.say: You set the course and never let go of the wheel. The market hasn't moved and you've already moved the stop three times.

AGQZ.title: The Clockmaker
AGQZ.say: Enter, exit, next one — like clockwork. You're not trading, you're clocking in.

AGQM.title: The Guerrilla
AGQM.say: Hit and run, and every hit gets two more touch-ups on the way out.

AXLZ.title: The Rock
AXLZ.say: "It'll come back." Place it, stop looking, never cut a loser. So far the market has been kind to you.

AXLM.title: The Negotiator
AXLM.say: When the stop gets close, you nudge it back a little. That's not a stop loss, that's haggling with the market.

AXQZ.title: The Blade
AXQZ.say: Ten small wins, one loss that pays them all back.

AXQM.title: The Striker
AXQM.say: Hands faster than your head, always tweaking — but you can't bring yourself to cut the losers.

RGLZ.title: The Officer
RGLZ.say: You do exactly what the signal says and never touch it. But when did you last read a chart yourself?

RGLM.title: The Tuner
RGLM.say: Whatever stop and target the signal gives, you always give them another twist.

RGQZ.title: The Stickler
RGQZ.say: Lots of trades, no improvising, out on schedule. So steady someone should pay you a salary.

RGQM.title: The Prober
RGQM.say: You follow, but never quite trust it: the stop gets twisted the moment you're in.

RXLZ.title: The Half-Believer
RXLZ.say: You trust the signal on direction and yourself on take-profit. You win pocket change and lose round numbers.

RXLM.title: The Windrider
RXLM.say: You trust the signal's direction completely; its stop loss is up for negotiation.

RXQZ.title: The Hitchhiker
RXQZ.say: You hitch a ride on the signal and hop off after a small gain — but never hop off when it's losing.

RXQM.title: The Surfer
RXQM.say: Lots of follows, lots of edits. A busy day, and your account didn't feel a thing.

intro.title: How the trading persona works
intro.how: We look at your live trades on this platform over the last 90 days and pick one letter on each of four axes — judgement, risk, tempo and management. The four letters make your code; there are 16 in all. It is recalculated on the 1st of each month and stays a first read until 50 trades.
